data.name: Feerozaht
data.gender_notes: Feerozaht is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name of divine origin meaning 'Bright and Shining One'. This name is often given to a child born during a time of spiritual enlightenment, or to one who is believed to bring light and radiance to the world. The name Feerozaht carries the meaning “Bright and Shining One” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Pashto. Parents who choose Feerozaht usually hope their child will grow to embody bright and shining one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name inspired by the divine light of Allah, symbolizing a pure and gentle soul.
data.etymology: Feerozaht belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Bright and Shining One.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Feerozaht total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Feerozaht holds deep cultural significance as it is derived from the Persian language, where 'feer' means 'light' and 'oz' means 'shining'. This name is revered in various Islamic communities, particularly those with Persian or Indian origins, as it symbolizes the triumph of light over darkness. It is a name that evokes imagery of purity, grace, and the supreme power of Allah.
data.spiritual_significance: Feerozaht is a name deeply rooted in spiritual symbolism, and is believed to be a blessing from Allah for the child bearer. The name signifies the child as a beacon of hope and light, often used as a reminder of the verse from the Quran, "Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is as if there is a Niche and within it a Lamp: the Lamp enclosed in Glass: the glass as it were a glowing star from the world of Sha'hwaar [i.e., a heavenly tree known as the Naft janah under which the prophets Ada and Hawwa lived]. From this Lamp are lit branches extending illumine the whole length of [Mount] Safa and Marwah. The Tafassun [i.e., splitting of the Lamp's light into many lights] is compared to the angels who are descended from the Right Hand [i.e., the angels of mercy] and the left Hand [i.e., the angels of inspiration]. And it is He Who sends down the Spirit [Gabriel] upon His Servant [Prophet Muhammad] as He willed. Sufficient for you is this knowledge, O Muhammad, and sufficient is Allah as a Witness" [Ibn 'Abbas reported: This hadith is called ra'yat an-nar, i.e., the description of the Divine Light]."
